name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
title: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
answer: Sales, use, and value added tax are transaction taxes that apply to the transfer of goods and services. Sales tax is imposed by state and local jurisdictions in the United States, use tax complements it when sales tax was not collected, and value added tax is a multi-stage tax used in many other countries. The scope covers taxability rules, rates, exemptions, nexus, and place of supply, which determine who must collect and remit. It also covers the documentation and filing obligations that follow from those determinations.

sections.body: Sales, use, and value added tax are transaction taxes that apply to the transfer of goods and services. Sales tax is imposed by state and local jurisdictions in the United States, use tax complements it when sales tax was not collected, and value added tax is a multi-stage tax used in many other countries. The scope covers taxability rules, rates, exemptions, nexus, and place of supply, which determine who must collect and remit. It also covers the documentation and filing obligations that follow from those determinations.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on transaction data from billing, e-commerce, and enterprise resource planning systems. Tax determination engines apply jurisdiction rules and rate tables to each line item, and exemption certificate databases hold customer status. Filing and remittance platforms connect to general ledgers and reporting tools. Some teams add AI tools for classification, anomaly detection, and data cleanup, but the core remains the tax engine and the underlying records.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins with nexus analysis and product or service classification. Each item is mapped to a tax category, then place of supply rules determine the jurisdiction and rate. Exemption certificates are validated, tax is calculated, and returns are prepared and filed. For VAT, the method also tracks input tax credits and reverse charge mechanisms. Reconciliation and audit trails are maintained throughout.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on audit exposure, penalties, and interest for incorrect collection or remittance. Provenance matters because tax authorities expect a clear record of source data, rule versions, and who approved each determination. Exemption certificates must be valid and retained, and customer data must be handled under privacy rules. AI-generated determinations need human review and documented reasoning to be defensible. Taxpayers have rights to appeal assessments and claim refunds, but those rights depend on timely and accurate records.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Jurisdictions continue to expand taxability to digital services and remote sellers, and e-invoicing and real-time reporting mandates are spreading. AI is increasingly used for real-time determination, risk scoring, and anomaly detection in returns. Tax authorities are also using data analytics to spot gaps, which raises the bar for documentation. The direction is toward more automated, continuous compliance with less reliance on periodic filing. Cross-border VAT rules for digital supplies are likely to keep changing.
